raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the left hemithorax with contralateral (rightward) tracheal deviation, which is the classic radiographic sign of a massive pleural effusion rather than lung collapse (which would cause ipsilateral deviation). Among the choices, only options A and C describe this correct mass-effect relationship, and pleural metastases are a far more common cause of such findings than pleural lymphoma.
